title: A Means of Assessing Maximal Oxygen Intake: Correlation Between Field and Treadmill Testing
claims: One hundred and fifteen US Air Force male officers and airmen completed a 12-minute field performance test and a treadmill maximal oxygen consumption test.
The correlation between 12-minute run distance and laboratory-determined maximal oxygen consumption was 0.897.
The author proposed that maximal oxygen consumption could be estimated from the 12-minute performance test.
The sample was limited to young military men, so the equation cannot be assumed to apply unchanged to other populations.

claimVerification.note: 原文：“One hundred and fifteen US Air Force male officers and airmen were evaluated on a 12-minute field performance test and on a treadmill maximal-oxygen-consumption test.”
原文：“The correlation of the field-test data with the laboratory-determined oxygen-consumption data was 0.897.”
原文：“The significance of this relationship makes it possible to estimate with considerable accuracy the maximal oxygen consumption from only the results of the 12-minute performance test.”

原文：“Since the majority of the subjects tested were less than 25 years of age, it is difficult to predict the accuracy of this test in an older age group.”样本均为 USAF 男性（平均 22 岁，17–52 岁）；原文仅就年龄与动机讨论外推限制，未单独讨论女性或其他人群。
